cards.text: Jesus has a message for seven churches, and John is the one holding the pen. First up: the angel of the church in Ephesus. John, I hope you stretched, because that's a LOT of dictation and there's NO backspace on a scroll.

cards.question: At the start of the Ephesus letter, Jesus describes Himself as the One who holds the seven ___ in His right hand and walks among the seven golden lampstands.

cards.text: Jesus tells Ephesus He knows their deeds, their labor and their perseverance. That's your boss stopping by your desk saying, 'I saw your work this week,' and for one long second you don't know if it's a raise or a MEETING.

cards.question: True or false: Jesus says the church in Ephesus puts up with people who are evil.
Some people came to the church in Ephesus falsely claiming to be apostles. What did the church do with them?

answers.text: Tested them and exposed them as liars
Let them teach the whole church

cards.text: They've persevered and endured many things without growing weary. Baker, I get winded hopping from one oven to the NEXT, and I'm hauling a gold base the whole way.

cards.question: The church in Ephesus has endured many things without growing weary. For the sake of what?

cards.text: So far this letter reads like Employee of the Month. Then Jesus says, 'But I have this against you:' and all of Ephesus leans in real slow.

cards.question: What does Jesus hold against the church in Ephesus?

answers.text: They have abandoned their first love
They have grown tired of serving

cards.text: Jesus tells them to keep in mind how far they've fallen. Then He shows them the way back.

cards.question: Jesus tells Ephesus to ___ and perform the deeds they did at ___.

cards.text: Then comes the warning: if they don't repent, Jesus will come to them. That's the line where the whole kitchen goes quiet and even the timer stops ticking.

cards.question: If Ephesus doesn't repent, Jesus will come and remove their ___ from its place.

cards.text: But Jesus gives them one more thing to their credit. They hate the works of the Nicolaitans.

cards.question: True or false: Jesus says He hates the works of the Nicolaitans too.

cards.text: Then Jesus says, 'He who has an ear, let him hear what the Spirit says to the churches.' Friend, that's not 'skim it later.' That's PUT. THE PHONE. DOWN.

cards.question: Jesus makes a promise to the one who overcomes. In the Paradise of God, they'll have the right to eat from what?

cards.text: Letter number two goes to the angel of the church in Smyrna. This time Jesus calls Himself the First and the Last.

cards.question: In the letter to Smyrna, Jesus also describes Himself by something He went through. What is it?

answers.text: He died and returned to life
He was driven into the desert

cards.text: Jesus tells Smyrna He knows their affliction and their poverty. And friend, I know a little about being cheap: my first price tag said 25 CENTS, and Mother Miller paid for me with one quarter and a smile.

cards.question: True or false: Jesus calls the poor church in Smyrna rich.

cards.text: Jesus is also aware of the slander from those who falsely claim to be Jews. He says they are in fact a synagogue of Satan.
Then Jesus tells Smyrna straight: suffering is coming.

cards.question: Suffering is coming for the church in Smyrna. What does Jesus tell them about it?

cards.text: And He gets specific. The devil is about to throw some of them into prison.

cards.question: Jesus says the devil will throw some of the church in Smyrna into prison. Why?
Jesus tells Smyrna they will suffer tribulation for ___ days.
Jesus tells Smyrna to be faithful even unto death, and He will give them the ___ of life.

cards.text: Then that line again: 'He who has an ear, let him hear what the Spirit says to the churches.'

cards.question: True or false: Jesus says the one who overcomes will not be harmed by the second death.

cards.text: Two letters down, FIVE churches to go, and I bet John's hand is already cramping. Trust me, friend, Jesus isn't done talking yet.

findings.problem: The card states facts from outside the passage: Jesus has a message for seven churches, and John is the one writing it down (Revelation 1:11, 19). The card cites only Revelation 2:1, so these facts have no reference.

rule.text: Facts from outside the passage are fine when they help, like who a new person is or who wrote a letter, with their reference.

findings.problem: The fill in the blank asks the baker to supply the wording of Jesus' self-description ('holds the seven ___ in His right hand'). No earlier card in this lesson mentions stars, so the baker can only guess a word they haven't seen. The card doesn't test meaning they can reason out.

rule.text: The rule against guessing the next words of a line (see below) applies to every passage, and to fill in the blank too. The blank tests meaning the baker can reason out, not wording they haven't seen.

findings.problem: The wrong answer 'They have grown tired of serving' is already ruled out by the setup. Card 6 and card 7's question both say the church endured 'without growing weary.' That leaves the card as a choice between two answers.

rule.text: A setup line can't rule out the wrong answers either.

findings.problem: The joke's comparison doesn't share the core action of the fact. Smyrna's poverty means having little. Papa Dorin's 25-cent price tag means being priced low or 'cheap.' Being poor and being cheap are different things, so the comparison doesn't click right away.

rule.text: The everyday comparison must have the same action.

findings.problem: The fill in the blank asks the baker to finish a set phrase ('the ___ of life') by guessing its wording. The wrong answers 'book' and 'bread' are also real '___ of life' phrases from Scripture, so nothing in the earlier cards lets the baker reason out 'crown.'

rule.text: Never ask the baker to guess the next words of a line.
